title: Fourier family size bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $s\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. If the Fourier $1$-norm of the real-valued version of $f$ is at most $s$, then the number of subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfying $(\varepsilon/4)\leq \|\widehat f\|_1|\widehat f(S)|$ is at most $\max\{1,\lceil 4s^2/\varepsilon\rceil\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
the Fourier $1$-norm of the real-valued version of $f$ is at most $s$
